rules.name: Major version in the URI path
rules.rationale: A visible major version in the path (/v2/...) lets consumers pin to a stable contract and lets us evolve without silently breaking them.

rules.name: Every operation is tagged
rules.rationale: Tags are how our docs, catalog, and SDK generators group operations. Untagged operations fall out of the developer experience.

rules.name: Every secured operation declares OAuth scopes
rules.rationale: Scopes are the coarse, auditable handle on what a token may do. An operation behind OAuth with no declared scope can't be reasoned about or least-privileged.
rules.roadmap: Aligning scope names on a shared resource:action convention — see the domain-grown oauth-scope-naming rule proposed for promotion.

rules.name: 4xx/5xx responses use the shared Problem schema
rules.rationale: One machine-readable error shape (RFC 9457 problem+json) means clients handle failures the same way across every API.

rules.name: No HTTP Basic authentication
rules.rationale: Basic ships long-lived credentials on every request. Everything new must use OAuth 2.1 or mTLS.

rules.name: Collection endpoints use cursor pagination
rules.rationale: Cursor pagination stays correct as data changes under the reader; offset pagination silently skips and repeats rows at scale.

rules.name: Unsafe methods support idempotency
rules.rationale: A retried POST should not create two resources. We recommend an idempotency key on unsafe methods.
rules.roadmap: Planned to move from info to warn in the next baseline release now that Payments has proven the pattern.

rules.name: Deprecated operations carry a Sunset header
rules.rationale: A machine-readable Sunset date (RFC 8594) gives consumers a countdown instead of a surprise 410.

adoptions.reason: Financial clients reconcile on machine-readable errors; a soft warning isn't enough.
Ledger and transaction listings must not skip or repeat rows under concurrent writes.
Double-charge protection is non-negotiable — an idempotency key is mandatory on every money-moving call.
No deprecated payment operations yet; will adopt when the first one lands.

adoptions.name: Mutations require an Idempotency-Key header
adoptions.rationale: Every POST/PATCH/DELETE must accept and honor an Idempotency-Key header so a retried request is safe.

adoptions.name: Monetary amounts are integers in minor units
adoptions.rationale: Amounts are integer minor units with an ISO 4217 currency — never floats — to avoid rounding drift.

adoptions.reason: Adopting next quarter once our token endpoints support retry keys.
Auth endpoints are versioned wholesale, not deprecated per-operation.

adoptions.name: Scopes follow a resource:action naming convention
adoptions.rationale: Scope strings must be resource:action (e.g. accounts:read) so they are self-describing, greppable, and consistent across every domain.

adoptions.reason: Public consumers we don't control can't be broken silently — an unversioned path fails the build.
Many public read endpoints are intentionally unauthenticated open data, so a hard error produces false positives; we warn and review.
A public API with no reachable owner is a support incident waiting to happen — contact info is required, not advisory.
Waiting on the shared Sunset middleware before enforcing.

adoptions.name: Scopes follow a resource:action naming convention
adoptions.rationale: We adopted the same resource:action scope convention Identity uses so our public scopes read the same way.

adoptions.reason: 40 SOAP-era services version in the query string; documented deviation, no reflow planned this year.
These services authenticate with gateway-issued API keys, not OAuth; scopes don't apply.
Two internal services still use Basic behind mTLS; migration is tracked and warn keeps it visible without blocking.
Offset pagination is baked into shipped desktop clients we can't update.
